name: daniela morales lopez

family.story: a comfortable family in Lima, mother and father, 1 older sibling

milestones.question: daniela is six. school is free here. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: it is what families like theirs do
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose play outside with the street kids. the parents decided: it is what families like theirs do

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise daniela with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family is managing. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose stay in school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i don't want to get into bad habits now and i value my health and community more. plus, joining a sports team sounds fun and will help me stay active.
milestones.thought: just another day saying no, back to the team for practice after school.
outcome: found a team and a habit
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and join a sports team over say no and go home, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken the

milestones.question: you are 17, with 12 years of school, in Lima. which path?
milestones.reasoning: i need to earn money right now to cover my expenses and help my family.
milestones.thought: another day at the factory, just trying to make ends meet today.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose take the factory job now over university, i need to earn money right now to cover my expenses and help my family

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: i need the emotional support and it's only $122 left over anyway.
milestones.thought: today i called renata and ximena. they made me laugh and feel better about everything.
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose keep up with close friends over work extra shifts, because an earlier life learned: keep at least one close friend throughout your life for support and companionship.

milestones.question: you are 24. stay in Lima or go?
milestones.reasoning: stay in lima, near family. it's important to be close to them and help out.
milestones.thought: today was just another day, spent with ximena making sure she had enough for the week. 🏡
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose stay in lima, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: i need to focus on saving and my family first. we don't have much, and i want to make sure we're okay before thinking about a relationship.
milestones.thought: today, i prayed for my family and saved more. it's hard, but necessary.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: ximena died, my mother. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i need their support now more than ever. we're in this together.
milestones.thought: today was hard, but talking with renata made everything feel a little lighter.
milestones.caption: 2053 · grief. chose lean on friends and family over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: keep at least one close friend throughout your life for support and companionship.

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: can't afford it now and need to save more. plus, i want to focus on my career and friendships first.
milestones.thought: pero si renata se ofrece a ayudar, quizás pueda esperar un poco más... 5 meses más de ahorro y estaré lista para un nuevo comienzo.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you earn about $420 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to save for future needs and reduce stress during periods of unrest.
milestones.thought: just saved a bit more today, daniela. hope it’s enough for when things get tough again.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose save a tenth every month over enjoy it now, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: money is tight this month and my body just isn't feeling great. i need to save for something more pressing.
milestones.thought: today was hard. worked all day, then had to skip the usual walk home because of the aches. maybe next week if i can afford it.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose no time for that, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and stay active. physical activity keeps the mind and body strong for years to come.

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Lima. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to miss work and risking injury could cost me more in the long run. my family needs my income.
milestones.thought: another day, another dollar saved for the kids' future.
milestones.caption: 2058 · the protest. chose stay home, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
milestones.world: in Latin America public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: you work as factory worker. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i can barely make ends meet as is. training or switching jobs would require time and money i don't have right now. starting a business seems too risky with my current savings. staying here means i'm providing for my family, even if it's just the basics.
milestones.thought: another day of work, another step closer to keeping up with rent and food. sometimes you just have to do what you can, no matter how small.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose stay put, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i need to save money for my father and sister. we don't have much, and i can only help by keeping my savings intact.
milestones.thought: just another day at the factory, praying for better times ahead.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose family comes first, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Lima. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i need to save money and stay safe. the unrest is high, and i don't want to risk getting hurt or arrested.
milestones.thought: another quiet day at home with a book, maybe some soup for dinner. sometimes peace means just being peaceful.
milestones.caption: 2068 · the protest. chose stay home, i need to save money and stay safe. the unrest is high, and i don't want to risk getting hurt or arrested
milestones.world: in Latin America public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: faith gives me strength and community, especially with my family's history and current unrest.
milestones.thought: voluntad de santiago, hoy estuve en la iglesia y sentí a mamá y ximena conmigo. me siento fuerte compartiendo esto con otros.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, because an earlier life learned: when grief or hardship strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are 47. something feels off.
milestones.reasoning: can't afford regular checkups now; might save money but risk health later.
milestones.thought: another month without checkups, still feeling okay for now.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose ignore it, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
